content:
Wall Street ended a punishing week on Friday with a partial recovery. The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.09% to 24,579.42 and the S&P 500 gained 0.31% to 7,376.86, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.46% on November 6. The S&P 500 was still on track for its worst week since June.

Thursday did the damage. The S&P 500 fell more than 4%, its worst day since the April 2025 tariff crash, and about $3 trillion in market value disappeared. The PHLX Semiconductor Index dropped 12%, its worst day since March 2020, and the Nasdaq slipped into a correction.

The trigger was political. After Tuesday's election, Democratic gains raised fears of tighter rules on AI data centers, Reuters reported on November 6, and investors worried that new rules could slow data center construction. For the week, technology stocks fell 7% and energy stocks fell 11%.

Volatility spiked along with prices. The VVIX rose as much as 70% on Thursday, a move seen only eight times since 1991, according to CBOE data cited by Yahoo Finance's Brian Sozzi. In the eight earlier cases, the S&P 500 averaged a 3.0% gain one month later and 14.7% one year later. You might also be interested in reading our piece on oversold AI stocks where Wall Street analysts are spotting 50%+ upside .

A Hot Jobs Report Revives Rate-Hike Bets

Friday's October jobs report added a second jolt. Employers added 165,000 jobs, more than twice what economists expected, and the unemployment rate ticked down to 4.1%, Reuters reported. Markets priced about a 78% chance of a quarter-point hike at the Federal Reserve's December meeting, up from about 67% a day earlier.

Fitch Ratings analyst Olu Sonola said the economy "remains on firm footing," and that the labor market's resilience pushes the debate toward a December hike. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, who has advocated further hikes, called inflation "a regressive tax, a distortionary tax." Our analysis of 52-week low technology stocks to buy according to analysts covers another group.

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said last month that policymakers would watch "the accumulation of data" to decide whether more tightening is needed. The 10-year Treasury yield was about 4.86% on Friday, up roughly 2 basis points. The Fed meets December 8-9, and a quarter-point hike is the widely expected outcome.

We shared the expanded list of 10 Stocks Getting Major Upgrades From Top Analysts here . You can find the top 5 stocks below.

Photo by Pascal Bernardon on Unsplash

For this article, we reviewed analyst upgrades issued on Friday, November 6, 2026, excluding new coverage initiations, and kept stocks listed on US exchanges whose ratings came from firms we track. We ranked the 10 stocks in ascending order of average upside potential, based on the average price target of all analysts covering the stock, as of November 7, 2026. We also list each stock's number of hedge fund holders as of Q2 2026, from our database of 1,006 hedge funds.

Don't Miss Out: 5 Stocks Getting Major Upgrades From Top Analysts

5. Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile (NYSE:SQM)

JPMorgan analyst Lucas Ferreira upgraded the Chilean lithium and chemicals producer Sociedad Química y Minera to Overweight from Neutral on November 6 and cut his fair value estimate to $71 from $88.

JPMorgan expects an "earnings reset" at the lithium and chemicals producer.

SQM's second-quarter revenue was $2.47 billion, up 136.7% from $1.04 billion a year earlier, and net income was $660.0 million, or $2.31 per share, compared with $88.4 million, or $0.31 per share, in the second quarter of 2025. Lithium sales volumes set a record at more than 84 thousand metric tons of lithium carbonate equivalent, 59% above the second quarter of 2025. Given current market conditions, the company expects lithium prices to stay relatively stable in the third quarter, and it expects full-year specialty plant nutrition volumes to rise about 10% versus 2025. It forecasts 280,000 to 290,000 metric tons of lithium carbonate equivalent from Novandino in 2026, and about $3 billion of capital spending over 2026 to 2028.

Whether lithium's downturn was over was the question in our article on SQM's earnings beat and raised lithium outlook .

TD Cowen analyst Menno Hulshof upgraded Baytex Energy, the Canadian oil and gas producer, to Buy from Hold on November 6 with a price target of C$8.

Hulshof described the company's growth plan as "thoughtful" and said it has "optionality." He also said the recent drop in the share price offers "an attractive entry point" for investors.

For the third quarter, Baytex reported petroleum and natural gas sales of C$605.9 million and production of 71,606 barrels of oil equivalent a day, 5% above a year earlier. At the end of September it had net cash of C$522.4 million, against net debt of C$2,244.4 million twelve months before. Its U.S. business was sold in December 2025. Free cash flow was C$138.5 million, and shareholder returns in the quarter totaled C$165 million, of which C$149 million went to buybacks.

Baytex raised its 2026 capital budget to about C$665 million and left production guidance at about 71,000 barrels a day. It guided 2027 production to 76,000 to 79,000 barrels a day, growth of 7% to 11%. Its Duvernay production hit a record 12,806 barrels a day, up 26%.

Seaport Global analyst Jay Goldberg upgraded SiTime to Buy from Neutral on November 6 and set a price target of $425.

Goldberg said the recent sell-off in AI-related stocks was too broad and went too far, which he sees as a buying opportunity in the timing solutions company. Seaport said it had stayed on the sidelines earlier because of valuation concerns. The upgrade came after a dip in the shares following earnings.

SiTime makes silicon-based timing parts that replace traditional quartz components. It reported third-quarter results after the market closed on November 4: net revenue was $298.7 million, up 257% from $83.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. Gross
